label: Trim columns from a CSV file in AWS S3 and upload the result
description: Every time a button is clicked, take an object called 'offices.csv' from AWS S3 with the key 'files/offices.csv'. Reduce number of columns in the csv file to ['F-NOM0103','F-COD0047','F-LOC0001','NUM0366']. Upload the file

tasks.label: Retrieve an object from AWS S3
tasks.name: awsS3_1
tasks.description: Downloads files/offices.csv from your S3 bucket. Change the key if your file is somewhere else.

tasks.label: Turn the csv file into a data pill
tasks.description: Parses the downloaded CSV, using its first row as the header, into a list of rows that the loop goes through.
tasks.name: csvFile_1

tasks.label: Loop over the csv items
tasks.description: Goes through each CSV row and keeps only the four columns the output file needs.
tasks.name: loop_1

iteratee.label: Create a data pill object for csv row
iteratee.name: var_1
iteratee.description: Builds a new row object containing only the F-NOM0103, F-COD0047, F-LOC0001 and NUM0366 columns from the current row.

iteratee.label: Store the variable object data pill into a list
iteratee.name: dataStorage_1
iteratee.description: Appends the trimmed row to the list stored under the key list for this run.

tasks.label: Get a variable object
tasks.name: dataStorage_2
tasks.description: Reads back the full list of trimmed rows once the loop has finished.

tasks.label: Convert a data pill into a csv file
tasks.description: Writes the trimmed rows into a new CSV file, file.csv.
tasks.name: csvFile_2

tasks.label: Put the csv file into AWS S3
tasks.name: awsS3_2
tasks.description: Uploads the trimmed CSV to S3 as files/offices_reduced.csv, as a private object.
